concepts.name: Scarcity
concepts.definition: Scarcity means resources are limited relative to unlimited wants, and scarcity creates the need for choice.

concepts.name: Opportunity Cost
concepts.definition: Opportunity cost is the value of the next best alternative forgone when a choice is made.

concepts.name: Demand
concepts.definition: Demand is the quantity of a good or service consumers are willing and able to buy at different prices under specified conditions during a given period.

concepts.name: Supply
concepts.definition: Supply is the quantity of a good or service producers are willing and able to sell at different prices under specified conditions.

concepts.name: Market Equilibrium
concepts.definition: A simplified market equilibrium occurs where quantity demanded equals quantity supplied.

concepts.name: Inflation
concepts.definition: Inflation is a sustained increase in the general price level over time.

concepts.name: Unemployment
concepts.definition: Unemployment is a condition involving people who are available for and seeking work but do not currently have employment, subject to the statistical definition being used.

concepts.name: State
concepts.definition: A state is a political entity generally characterized by territory, population, government, and sovereignty.

concepts.name: Democracy
concepts.definition: Democracy is a system in which political authority is exercised directly or through representatives under an established institutional framework.

concepts.name: Constitution
concepts.definition: A constitution is a fundamental framework establishing institutions, powers, rights, and rules of governance.

concepts.name: Separation of Powers
concepts.definition: Government functions may be distributed among legislature, executive, and judiciary, and separation of powers distributes governmental functions to reduce concentration of authority.

concepts.name: Rule of Law
concepts.definition: The rule of law is the principle that laws and legal institutions govern public authority and are applied through established legal processes.

concepts.name: Citizenship
concepts.definition: Citizenship is legal membership in a state, associated with rights and duties under that state's law.

concepts.name: Parts of Speech
concepts.definition: Common parts of speech include noun, pronoun, verb, adjective, adverb, preposition, conjunction, interjection, and determiner.

concepts.name: Sentence Types
concepts.definition: Common sentence types are declarative, interrogative, imperative, and exclamatory.

concepts.name: Declarative
concepts.definition: A declarative sentence makes a statement.

concepts.name: Interrogative
concepts.definition: An interrogative sentence asks a question.

concepts.name: Imperative
concepts.definition: An imperative sentence gives a command or instruction.

concepts.name: Exclamatory
concepts.definition: An exclamatory sentence expresses strong feeling.

concepts.name: Clauses
concepts.definition: Clauses are classified as independent clauses, which can function as complete sentences, and dependent clauses, which cannot normally stand alone as complete sentences.

concepts.name: Independent Clause
concepts.definition: An independent clause can function as a complete sentence.

concepts.name: Dependent Clause
concepts.definition: A dependent clause cannot normally stand alone as a complete sentence.

concepts.name: Figures of Speech
concepts.definition: Common figures of speech include simile, metaphor, personification, hyperbole, irony, oxymoron, alliteration, and onomatopoeia.

concepts.name: Simile
concepts.definition: Simile is one of the common figures of speech listed alongside metaphor, personification, hyperbole, irony, oxymoron, alliteration, and onomatopoeia.

concepts.name: Metaphor
concepts.definition: Metaphor is a common figure of speech, listed alongside simile, personification, hyperbole, irony, oxymoron, alliteration, and onomatopoeia.

concepts.name: Personification
concepts.definition: Personification is one of the common figures of speech.

concepts.name: Hyperbole
concepts.definition: Hyperbole is one of the common figures of speech.

concepts.name: Irony
concepts.definition: Irony is a contrast between appearance or expectation and reality, with different forms, and it is one of the common figures of speech.

concepts.name: Oxymoron
concepts.definition: Oxymoron is one of the common figures of speech.

concepts.name: Alliteration
concepts.definition: Alliteration is one of the common figures of speech.

concepts.name: Onomatopoeia
concepts.definition: Onomatopoeia is one of the common figures of speech.

concepts.name: Interjection
concepts.definition: Interjection is one of the common categories of parts of speech.

concepts.name: Determiner
concepts.definition: Determiner is one of the common categories of parts of speech.

concepts.name: Prose
concepts.definition: Prose is ordinary written language, including forms such as novels and short stories.

concepts.name: Poetry
concepts.definition: Poetry is literary expression that often uses rhythm, imagery, sound, structure, and condensed language.

concepts.name: Drama
concepts.definition: Drama is literature intended for performance.

concepts.name: Literary Elements
concepts.definition: Literary elements include plot, character, setting, theme, conflict, point of view, tone, mood, symbolism, and imagery.

concepts.name: Plot
concepts.definition: Plot is the sequence of events in a work of literature, commonly developed through exposition, rising action, climax, falling action, and resolution.

concepts.name: Character
concepts.definition: Character is one of the literary elements of a work; the exposition introduces the relevant characters, and a writer develops characters through characterization.

concepts.name: Setting
concepts.definition: Setting is one of the literary elements of a work, and the exposition introduces the relevant setting, characters, and situation.

concepts.name: Theme
concepts.definition: Theme is the central idea explored by a work of literature; it is one of the literary elements.

concepts.name: Conflict
concepts.definition: Conflict is one of the literary elements of a work, listed alongside plot, character, setting, theme, point of view, tone, mood, symbolism, and imagery.

concepts.name: Point of View
concepts.definition: Point of view is one of the literary elements of a work, listed alongside plot, character, setting, theme, conflict, tone, mood, symbolism, and imagery.

concepts.name: Tone
concepts.definition: Tone is the writer's or speaker's attitude, and it is one of the literary elements.

concepts.name: Mood
concepts.definition: Mood is the emotional atmosphere experienced by the reader or audience, and it is one of the literary elements.

concepts.name: Symbolism
concepts.definition: Symbolism is one of the literary elements of a work, listed alongside plot, character, setting, theme, conflict, point of view, tone, mood, and imagery.

concepts.name: Imagery
concepts.definition: Imagery is one of the literary elements of a work, and poetry often uses imagery along with rhythm, sound, structure, and condensed language.

concepts.name: Old Testament Topics
concepts.definition: Old Testament topics include Creation, Fall, Noah, Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, Joseph, Moses, Exodus, Ten Commandments, Judges, Kings, Prophets, and Wisdom literature, with core categories also covering Covenant, Patriarchs, Law, and Kingdom.

concepts.name: New Testament Topics
concepts.definition: New Testament topics include the birth and ministry of Jesus, teachings, parables, miracles, disciples, passion, resurrection, Great Commission, Pentecost, early church, and Pauline ministry, with core categories also covering the life and teachings of Jesus and death and resurrection.

concepts.name: Christian Ethics
concepts.definition: Christian ethics includes love, forgiveness, justice, mercy, honesty, service, humility, stewardship, and faithfulness, and is a core Christian Religious Studies knowledge category.

concepts.name: Faith
concepts.definition: Faith is a core Christian Religious Studies knowledge category and a value within Christian ethics.

concepts.name: Love
concepts.definition: Love is a core Christian Religious Studies knowledge category and a value within Christian ethics.

concepts.name: Forgiveness
concepts.definition: Forgiveness is a core Christian Religious Studies knowledge category and a value within Christian ethics.

concepts.name: Service
concepts.definition: Service is a core Christian Religious Studies knowledge category and a value within Christian ethics.

concepts.name: Leadership
concepts.definition: Leadership is a core Christian Religious Studies knowledge category.

concepts.name: Denominational Interpretation
concepts.definition: When answering denominational or interpretive questions, distinguish biblical text, historical interpretation, denominational interpretation, and personal interpretation.

concepts.name: Business Model
concepts.definition: A business model describes how an organization creates, delivers, and captures value.

concepts.name: Value Proposition
concepts.definition: A value proposition explains why a target customer might choose a product or service.

concepts.name: Customer Segments
concepts.definition: Customer segments are groups of customers with relevant shared needs or characteristics.

concepts.name: Cost
concepts.definition: Cost is the resources consumed to operate or produce.

concepts.name: Fixed Cost
concepts.definition: A fixed cost does not vary directly with short-term production volume in the simplified model.

concepts.name: Variable Cost
concepts.definition: A variable cost changes with production or activity level.

concepts.name: Gross Profit
concepts.definition: Gross profit is revenue minus cost of goods sold, under the relevant accounting framework.

concepts.name: Break-even
concepts.definition: Break-even is the point where total revenue equals total cost in a simplified model.

concepts.name: Marketing
concepts.definition: Marketing covers the activities used to communicate and deliver value to customers.

concepts.name: Branding
concepts.definition: Branding is the system of identity, associations, and experiences connected with an organization or product.

concepts.name: Product-Market Fit
concepts.definition: Product-market fit is the concept describing strong alignment between a product and a real market need.

concepts.name: MVP
concepts.definition: MVP means minimum viable product: the smallest useful version designed to test assumptions with users.

concepts.name: Customer Feedback
concepts.definition: Customer feedback is evidence used to improve product decisions.

concepts.name: Revenue
concepts.definition: Revenue is money earned by an organization and income from ordinary activities.

concepts.name: Assets
concepts.definition: Assets are resources controlled by an entity that have economic value.

concepts.name: Liabilities
concepts.definition: Liabilities are obligations.

concepts.name: Equity
concepts.definition: Equity is the residual interest after liabilities are deducted from assets.

concepts.name: Accounting Equation
concepts.definition: The accounting equation states that Assets = Liabilities + Equity.

concepts.name: Expense
concepts.definition: An expense is a cost incurred in generating revenue.

concepts.name: Profit
concepts.definition: Profit is revenue minus expenses under the applicable accounting definition.

concepts.name: Cash Flow
concepts.definition: Cash flow is the movement of cash into and out of an entity.

concepts.name: Budget
concepts.definition: A budget is planned income and expenditure.

concepts.name: Depreciation
concepts.definition: Depreciation is the systematic allocation of an asset's depreciable amount over its useful life.

concepts.name: Basic Economic Problem
concepts.definition: The basic economic problem is that scarcity creates the need for choice.

concepts.name: Factors of Production
concepts.definition: The factors of production are land, labour, capital, and entrepreneurship.

concepts.name: Utility
concepts.definition: Utility is the satisfaction derived from consumption.

concepts.name: Marginal Utility
concepts.definition: Marginal utility is the additional utility from one more unit.

concepts.name: Law of Demand
concepts.definition: The law of demand states that, ceteris paribus, quantity demanded generally decreases as price rises.

concepts.name: Law of Supply
concepts.definition: The law of supply states that, ceteris paribus, quantity supplied generally increases as price rises.

concepts.name: Elasticity
concepts.definition: Elasticity measures the responsiveness of one variable to another.

concepts.name: Price Elasticity of Demand
concepts.definition: Price elasticity of demand is the percentage change in quantity demanded divided by the percentage change in price.

concepts.name: GDP
concepts.definition: GDP is the market value of final goods and services produced within a geographic area during a specified period.

concepts.name: Nominal GDP
concepts.definition: Nominal GDP is measured at current prices.

concepts.name: Real GDP
concepts.definition: Real GDP is adjusted to remove the effect of price changes using an appropriate methodology.

concepts.name: Fiscal Policy
concepts.definition: Fiscal policy covers government decisions about taxation and expenditure.

concepts.name: Monetary Policy
concepts.definition: Monetary policy is central-bank policy affecting money, credit, interest rates, and related conditions.

concepts.name: Interest Rate
concepts.definition: An interest rate is the cost of borrowing or the return for lending or saving, depending on context.

concepts.name: Exchange Rate
concepts.definition: An exchange rate is the price of one currency in terms of another.

concepts.name: Balance of Payments
concepts.definition: The balance of payments is a systematic record of economic transactions between residents of an economy and the rest of the world.

concepts.name: Political Institutions
concepts.definition: Political institutions include the legislature, executive, and judiciary.

concepts.name: Legislature
concepts.definition: The legislature makes laws and performs representation and oversight functions within its constitutional framework.

concepts.name: Executive
concepts.definition: The executive implements laws and manages public administration.

concepts.name: Judiciary
concepts.definition: The judiciary interprets and applies law through courts.

concepts.name: Constitutionalism
concepts.definition: Constitutionalism means that government authority is constrained by constitutional rules.

concepts.name: Federalism
concepts.definition: Federalism is the constitutional division of powers between levels of government.

concepts.name: Unitary System
concepts.definition: In a unitary system, central government retains primary constitutional authority, with local administration delegated under the relevant system.

concepts.name: Checks and Balances
concepts.definition: Under checks and balances, institutions constrain one another through legally defined powers.

concepts.name: Election
concepts.definition: An election is the formal process through which voters select representatives or decide specified questions.

concepts.name: Political Party
concepts.definition: A political party is an organization that seeks to influence or obtain political power through electoral and political activity.

concepts.name: Civil Society
concepts.definition: Civil society comprises organizations and associations outside the state and family structures that participate in public life.

concepts.name: Human Rights
concepts.definition: Human rights are fundamental rights and freedoms recognized by applicable legal and international frameworks.

concepts.name: Geography of Nigeria
concepts.definition: Nigeria is located in West Africa and has a coastline on the Gulf of Guinea.

concepts.name: Major Rivers
concepts.definition: Nigeria's major rivers are the Niger and the Benue.

concepts.name: Major Vegetation Belts
concepts.definition: Nigeria's major vegetation belts are mangrove/swamp, rainforest, Guinea savanna, Sudan savanna, and the Sahel transition in the far north.

concepts.name: Noun
concepts.definition: A noun names a person, place, thing, concept, or entity, and is one of the common parts of speech.

concepts.name: Pronoun
concepts.definition: A pronoun substitutes for a noun phrase.

concepts.name: Verb
concepts.definition: A verb expresses action, occurrence, or state.

concepts.name: Adjective
concepts.definition: An adjective modifies or describes a noun or noun phrase.

concepts.name: Adverb
concepts.definition: An adverb modifies a verb, adjective, adverb, clause, or sentence depending on use.

concepts.name: Preposition
concepts.definition: A preposition expresses relationships such as location, direction, time, or manner.

concepts.name: Conjunction
concepts.definition: A conjunction connects words, phrases, or clauses.

concepts.name: Tense
concepts.definition: Tense expresses temporal relationships through grammatical forms.

concepts.name: Active Voice
concepts.definition: In the active voice, the subject performs the action.

concepts.name: Passive Voice
concepts.definition: In the passive voice, the subject receives the action.

concepts.name: Direct Speech
concepts.definition: Direct speech reports exact wording as quoted.

concepts.name: Indirect Speech
concepts.definition: Indirect speech reports content without necessarily preserving exact wording.

concepts.name: Subject-Verb Agreement
concepts.definition: The verb form should agree appropriately with the grammatical subject.

concepts.name: Punctuation
concepts.definition: Common punctuation marks include the comma, period/full stop, colon, semicolon, question mark, exclamation mark, apostrophe, quotation marks, and parentheses.

concepts.name: Exposition
concepts.definition: The exposition introduces the relevant setting, characters, and situation.

concepts.name: Rising Action
concepts.definition: Rising action consists of developing complications in a plot.

concepts.name: Climax
concepts.definition: The climax is the major turning point or peak of dramatic tension.

concepts.name: Falling Action
concepts.definition: Falling action comprises the events following the climax.

concepts.name: Resolution
concepts.definition: Resolution is the outcome or conclusion of a work.

concepts.name: Characterization
concepts.definition: Characterization is how a writer develops characters.

concepts.name: Foreshadowing
concepts.definition: Foreshadowing gives hints about possible future events.

concepts.name: Flashback
concepts.definition: A flashback is a narrative shift to an earlier event.

concepts.name: Argument
concepts.definition: An argument is a set of premises intended to support a conclusion.

concepts.name: Premise
concepts.definition: A premise is a statement offered as support.

concepts.name: Conclusion
concepts.definition: A conclusion is a claim supported by premises.

concepts.name: Deductive Reasoning
concepts.definition: In deductive reasoning, if premises are true and reasoning is valid, the conclusion follows necessarily.

concepts.name: Inductive Reasoning
concepts.definition: Inductive reasoning uses observations or evidence to support a generalization without deductive certainty.

concepts.name: Correlation
concepts.definition: Correlation is a statistical association.

concepts.name: Causation
concepts.definition: Causation means one factor contributes to producing another under a defined causal model.

concepts.name: Common Fallacies
concepts.definition: Common fallacies include ad hominem, straw man, false dilemma, appeal to ignorance, hasty generalization, circular reasoning, slippery slope, and appeal to popularity.

concepts.name: Active Recall
concepts.definition: Active recall is the attempt to retrieve information from memory rather than merely rereading.

concepts.name: Spaced Repetition
concepts.definition: Spaced repetition is reviewing material at increasing intervals.

concepts.name: Interleaving
concepts.definition: Interleaving means mixing related problem types rather than practicing only one type at a time.

concepts.name: Elaboration
concepts.definition: Elaboration means explaining why or how information connects to other knowledge.

concepts.name: Practice Testing
concepts.definition: Practice testing uses questions to test retrieval and application.

concepts.name: Feynman-Style Explanation
concepts.definition: A Feynman-style explanation means explaining a concept in simple language, identifying gaps, then refining.

concepts.name: Error Log
concepts.definition: An error log records the question, the mistake, the correct method, why the mistake happened, and a prevention strategy.

concepts.name: Ancient Civilizations
concepts.definition: The ancient civilizations grouping covers Mesopotamia, Ancient Egypt, Ancient Greece, Ancient Rome, Indus Valley, Ancient China, and Mesoamerican civilizations as foundational history topics.

concepts.name: Mesopotamia
concepts.definition: Mesopotamia is one of the ancient civilizations covered in the history knowledge framework.

concepts.name: Ancient Egypt
concepts.definition: Ancient Egypt is one of the ancient civilizations covered in the history knowledge framework.

concepts.name: Ancient Greece
concepts.definition: Ancient Greece is one of the ancient civilizations covered in the history knowledge framework.

concepts.name: Ancient Rome
concepts.definition: Ancient Rome is one of the ancient civilizations covered in the history knowledge framework.

concepts.name: Indus Valley
concepts.definition: The Indus Valley is one of the ancient civilizations covered in the history knowledge framework.

concepts.name: Ancient China
concepts.definition: Ancient China is one of the ancient civilizations covered in the history knowledge framework.

concepts.name: Mesoamerican Civilizations
concepts.definition: Mesoamerican civilizations are one of the ancient civilization groupings covered in the history knowledge framework.

concepts.name: West African History
concepts.definition: West African history is a framework of useful topics covering ancient West African states, the Ghana, Mali, and Songhai empires, trade, regional states, colonialism, and independence movements.

concepts.name: Ancient West African States
concepts.definition: Ancient West African states are one of the useful topics listed in the West African history framework.

concepts.name: Ghana Empire
concepts.definition: The Ghana Empire is a West African state studied alongside the Mali and Songhai empires and Trans-Saharan trade in the West African history framework.

concepts.name: Mali Empire
concepts.definition: The Mali Empire is a West African empire studied alongside the Ghana and Songhai empires and Trans-Saharan trade in the West African history framework.

concepts.name: Songhai Empire
concepts.definition: The Songhai Empire is a West African empire studied alongside the Ghana and Mali empires and Trans-Saharan trade in the West African history framework.

concepts.name: Trans-Saharan Trade
concepts.definition: Trans-Saharan trade is a useful topic in the West African history framework, listed alongside the Ghana, Mali, and Songhai empires.

concepts.name: Kanem-Bornu
concepts.definition: Kanem-Bornu is one of the useful topics listed in the West African history framework.

concepts.name: Oyo
concepts.definition: Oyo is one of the useful topics listed in the West African history framework.

concepts.name: Benin
concepts.definition: Benin is one of the useful topics listed in the West African history framework.

concepts.name: Hausa City-States
concepts.definition: The Hausa city-states are one of the useful topics listed in the West African history framework.

concepts.name: African-European Trade
concepts.definition: African-European trade is a useful topic in the West African history framework, listed alongside colonialism and independence movements.

concepts.name: Colonialism
concepts.definition: Colonialism is a useful topic in the West African history framework, listed with African-European trade and independence movements.

concepts.name: Independence Movements
concepts.definition: Independence movements are a useful topic in the West African history framework, listed with colonialism and African-European trade.

concepts.name: Nigerian History Framework
concepts.definition: The Nigerian history framework covers precolonial societies, transatlantic trade, British colonial administration, amalgamation, nationalist movements, independence, constitutional development, post-independence political history, military and civilian periods, civil war, and the return to democratic governance.

concepts.name: Precolonial Societies
concepts.definition: Precolonial societies are a listed topic in the Nigerian history framework.

concepts.name: Transatlantic Trade
concepts.definition: Transatlantic trade is a listed topic in the Nigerian history framework.

concepts.name: British Colonial Administration
concepts.definition: British colonial administration is a listed topic in the Nigerian history framework.

concepts.name: Amalgamation
concepts.definition: Amalgamation is a listed topic in the Nigerian history framework.

concepts.name: Nationalist Movements
concepts.definition: Nationalist movements are a listed topic in the Nigerian history framework.

concepts.name: Independence
concepts.definition: Independence is a listed topic in the Nigerian history framework.

concepts.name: Constitutional Development
concepts.definition: Constitutional development is a listed topic in the Nigerian history framework.

concepts.name: Post-Independence Political History
concepts.definition: Post-independence political history is a listed topic in the Nigerian history framework.

concepts.name: Military/Civilian Periods
concepts.definition: Military and civilian periods are a listed topic in the Nigerian history framework.

concepts.name: Civil War
concepts.definition: Civil war is a listed topic in the Nigerian history framework.

concepts.name: Return to Democratic Governance
concepts.definition: The return to democratic governance is a listed topic in the Nigerian history framework.

concepts.name: Epistemology
concepts.definition: Epistemology is the study of knowledge, justification, and belief.

concepts.name: Ethics
concepts.definition: Ethics is the study of moral concepts and conduct.

concepts.name: Metaphysics
concepts.definition: Metaphysics is the study of fundamental questions about reality and existence.

concepts.name: Logical Validity
concepts.definition: Logical validity is an argument form that guarantees the conclusion from the premises if the premises are true.

concepts.name: Soundness
concepts.definition: Soundness is a valid argument with true premises.

concepts.name: Active Listening
concepts.definition: Active listening is the practice of understanding, clarifying, reflecting, and responding to a speaker.

concepts.name: Paraphrasing
concepts.definition: Paraphrasing is restating an idea using different wording while preserving meaning.

concepts.name: Ambiguity
concepts.definition: Ambiguity is a statement that admits multiple plausible interpretations.

concepts.name: Synonym
concepts.definition: A synonym is a word with a similar meaning.

concepts.name: Antonym
concepts.definition: An antonym is a word of opposite or contrasting meaning.

concepts.name: Hypernym
concepts.definition: A hypernym is a broader category; animal is the hypernym of dog.
examples: Animal is the hypernym of dog

concepts.name: Hyponym
concepts.definition: A hyponym is a more specific member of a category; dog is the hyponym of animal.
examples: Dog is the hyponym of animal

concepts.name: Homonym
concepts.definition: A homonym has the same form or sound with different meanings depending on the definition.

concepts.name: Polysemy
concepts.definition: Polysemy occurs when one word has multiple related meanings.

concepts.name: Market Structures
concepts.definition: Market structures include perfect competition, monopolistic competition, oligopoly, and monopoly.

concepts.name: Perfect Competition
concepts.definition: Perfect competition is one of the market structures covered in the advanced economics framework.

concepts.name: Monopolistic Competition
concepts.definition: Monopolistic competition is one of the market structures covered in the advanced economics framework.

concepts.name: Monopoly
concepts.definition: A monopoly is a single dominant seller under the simplified model, with significant barriers to entry.

concepts.name: Oligopoly
concepts.definition: An oligopoly is a market dominated by a small number of firms.

concepts.name: Externality
concepts.definition: An externality is the effect of an activity on third parties not fully reflected in market prices.

concepts.name: Public Good
concepts.definition: A public good is often characterized by non-rivalry and non-excludability in the idealized model.

concepts.name: Common Resource
concepts.definition: A common resource is difficult to exclude people from using and can be depleted by use.

concepts.name: Subsidy
concepts.definition: A subsidy is financial support that can lower effective cost or encourage an activity.

concepts.name: Price Ceiling
concepts.definition: A price ceiling is a legal maximum price.

concepts.name: Price Floor
concepts.definition: A price floor is a legal minimum price.

concepts.name: Market Research
concepts.definition: Market research collects evidence about customers, alternatives, needs, and market conditions.

concepts.name: Customer Persona
concepts.definition: A customer persona is a representative description of a target customer segment.

concepts.name: Pain Point
concepts.definition: A pain point is a problem or friction experienced by a customer.

concepts.name: Competitive Analysis
concepts.definition: Competitive analysis is the study of alternatives, differentiators, constraints, and market positioning.

concepts.name: Go-to-Market
concepts.definition: A go-to-market plan is a plan for launching and distributing a product.

concepts.name: Retention
concepts.definition: Retention is the ability to keep users or customers over time.

concepts.name: Churn
concepts.definition: Churn is the rate at which customers or users stop using a product or service.

concepts.name: Lifetime Value
concepts.definition: Lifetime value is the estimated economic value of a customer relationship under a chosen model.

concepts.name: Customer Acquisition Cost
concepts.definition: Customer acquisition cost is the cost associated with acquiring customers.

concepts.name: Project
concepts.definition: A project is a temporary effort intended to create a defined output.

concepts.name: Scope
concepts.definition: Scope is what is included and excluded in a project.

concepts.name: Milestone
concepts.definition: A milestone is a significant checkpoint.

concepts.name: Dependency
concepts.definition: A dependency is a relationship where one task relies on another.

concepts.name: Risk
concepts.definition: Risk is a potential uncertain event with impact.

concepts.name: Issue
concepts.definition: An issue is a problem currently occurring.

concepts.name: Backlog
concepts.definition: A backlog is an ordered list of pending work.

concepts.name: Sprint
concepts.definition: A sprint is a time-boxed development period in Scrum-style workflows.

concepts.name: Kanban
concepts.definition: Kanban is a visual workflow management approach.

concepts.name: Definition of Done
concepts.definition: The definition of done is agreed criteria for considering work complete.

concepts.name: Discovery
concepts.definition: Discovery is understanding the problem, users, and context before committing to solutions.

concepts.name: Prototype
concepts.definition: A prototype is a representation used to explore or test an idea.

concepts.name: Iteration
concepts.definition: Iteration is a cycle of build, observe, learn, and improve.

concepts.name: Regression
concepts.definition: Regression is a new change unintentionally breaking old behavior.

concepts.name: Feature
concepts.definition: A feature is a user-facing capability.

concepts.name: Tech Debt
concepts.definition: Tech debt is future cost created by expedient technical decisions.

concepts.name: Paragraph
concepts.definition: A paragraph usually has a topic or central idea, supporting details, coherence, and a closing or transition where needed.

concepts.name: Thesis
concepts.definition: A thesis is the central claim of an essay or argument.

concepts.name: Outline
concepts.definition: An outline is a plan of major sections before drafting.

concepts.name: Revision
concepts.definition: Revision improves content, logic, organization, and clarity.

concepts.name: Editing
concepts.definition: Editing corrects grammar, wording, consistency, and style.

concepts.name: Proofreading
concepts.definition: Proofreading is a final surface-level error check.

concepts.name: Tone
concepts.definition: Tone is the attitude conveyed by a text; in writing it may be formal, neutral, conversational, persuasive, academic, or friendly.

concepts.name: Slide Purpose
concepts.definition: Slide purpose is the principle that each slide should support one major idea where practical.

concepts.name: Good Structure
concepts.definition: A good presentation structure includes title, context, key message, evidence or example, and a conclusion or next step.

concepts.name: Data Visualization
concepts.definition: Data visualization means choosing a chart based on the question: bar to compare categories, line for trend over time, scatter for relationship, histogram for distribution, and pie for limited part-to-whole comparisons when appropriate; avoid misleading scales and unnecessary decoration.

concepts.name: Main Idea
concepts.definition: The main idea is the central point of a passage.

concepts.name: Detail
concepts.definition: A detail is supporting information in a passage.

concepts.name: Inference
concepts.definition: An inference is a conclusion supported by evidence but not directly stated.

concepts.name: Author's Purpose
concepts.definition: The author's purpose is the reason for creating the text.

concepts.name: Context
concepts.definition: Context is the information around a statement that helps interpret meaning.

concepts.name: Critical Reading
concepts.definition: Critical reading asks what the claim is, what evidence supports it, whether that evidence is relevant and sufficient, what assumptions and alternative explanations exist, whether the source is reliable, and what would disprove the claim.
